subject: Apollo astronauts quarantine trailer
title: What If Astronauts Brought Back Moon Germs? NASA Locked Them in a Trailer

scenes.text: What if astronauts brought back Moon germs? In 1969, NASA locked its heroes in a trailer.
Splashdown, July 24th, 1969. The crew pulled on rubber isolation suits and were scrubbed with disinfectant on the open sea.
Then 88 hours sealed in a 35-foot Airstream trailer, five men inside, shipped from Hawaii to Houston.
Twenty-one days in total. Meanwhile in the lab a glove ruptured and a sterilizer leaked, quarantining 24 more people.
And before any of it, the capsule had vented its cabin air during re-entry, then opened its hatch onto the Pacific.
A 2023 study concluded the quarantine looked like a success only because it was never needed. NASA dropped it after Apollo 14.

description:
What if the Apollo astronauts had brought back Moon microbes? After splashdown on 24 July 1969 the Apollo 11 crew wore isolation garments, spent about 88 hours in a converted Airstream trailer and finished a 21-day quarantine in Houston's Lunar Receiving Laboratory.
NASA's own history records a ruptured glove and an autoclave leak that put 24 staff into quarantine, and the capsule had already vented air during re-entry. A 2023 study in the journal Isis argued the protocol only looked like a success because it was not needed. Quarantine ended after Apollo 14.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: The crew also filled in a US customs form in Honolulu, declaring Moon rock and Moon dust. Would you have signed up for three weeks in a trailer? And what should we run through next?
